key_insight: OmniVerifier-M1 shows that verifier-generated rationales (not just binary decisions) plus an explicit structured recalibration mechanism yield much more reliable, fine-grained multimodal verification for visual outputs.
problem_solved: Addresses brittle, decision-only verification for multimodal LLMs by enabling models to use verifier rationales and symbolic outputs (e.g., bounding boxes, labels) as structured feedback to improve correctness, calibration, and explainability.
method: Multimodal meta-verifier: consumes image + text + verifier-generated rationales (textual explanations and symbolic outputs) to produce refined verification judgments.

Explicit Structured Recalibration (ESR): converts symbolic verifier outputs (bounding boxes, labels, attributes) into structured representations aligned with model latent space for targeted recalibration.
Meta-training loop: integrates rationale-based supervision and calibration/consistency losses so the verifier learns from explanations rather than only decisions.
impact: Enables finer-grained, better-calibrated verification of visual model outputs—improving trust, debuggability, and safety for practitioners deploying multimodal foundation models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: image+prompt → base multimodal model → verifier (rationale + symbolic outputs) → meta-verifier + ESR → recalibrated output
Before/after example: visualization showing original bounding boxes/labels vs. ESR-corrected results with rationale text bubbles
Bar/chart: calibration/error-rate comparison between decision-only verifiers and OmniVerifier-M1 (accuracy, calibration metrics)
Icon set: rationale speech bubble, bounding-box symbol, feedback loop arrow, and shield for safety/trust
paper_title: OmniVerifier-M1: Multimodal Meta-Verifier with Explicit Structured Recalibration
paper_authors: Xinchen Zhang, Bowei Liu, Jiale Liu, Chufan Shi, Yizhen Zhang
